# Artificial packed-absorber profile

## Question

How closely does the artificial absorber model reproduce the artificial
gas-phase $\mathrm{CO_2}$ observations over a packed height of
$0$ to $6\ \mathrm{m}$?

The comparison is deliberately synthetic. It demonstrates the analysis-notebook
view and does not validate a physical absorber model.

## Conditions

| Item | Retained condition |
|---|---|
| Quantity | Gas-phase $\mathrm{CO_2}$, percent by volume |
| Coordinate | Packed height, $0$ to $6\ \mathrm{m}$ |
| Model role | Continuous predicted profile |
| Observation role | Artificial point observations |
| Observation uncertainty | Assigned $\pm 0.30$ percentage points |
| Residual definition | $e_i=y_{i,\mathrm{model}}-y_{i,\mathrm{obs}}$ |
| Data authority | `../../data/artificial-absorber-profile.csv` |

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
```{=latex}
\clearpage
```
:::

## Numerical comparison

The retained residual column gives:

| Statistic | Value (percentage points) |
|---|---:|
| Root-mean-square residual | 0.165 |
| Mean absolute residual | 0.157 |
| Mean residual | -0.071 |
| Maximum absolute residual | 0.200 |

Every artificial residual is smaller in magnitude than the assigned observation
uncertainty. The model and observations therefore agree by construction for
this demonstration; the comparison establishes no physical-model accuracy.

## Interpretation and limitations

The artificial model reproduces the imposed decreasing profile across the
tested height range. The residuals include both signs and show no monotonic
drift in this seven-point example.

The values are fabricated, the uncertainty is assigned rather than measured,
and no code-verification, solution-verification, or physical-validation claim
follows. The example supports only the document workflow: one retained table,
one interpretation, and consistent PDF and HTML views.

## Conclusion and next steps

The retained synthetic values demonstrate consistent table, figure, PDF, and
HTML reporting without model execution. A real analysis should replace the
synthetic table with reviewed retained results and repeat the same numerical
and visual checks.
